findings.location: Results, Delphi-item ratings vs bp_work/results/final/0.main_table.csv column consensus (TRUE rows)

findings.question_for_authors: Which run produced the reported value of 'n items reaching consensus in Round 1' (26), given that bp_work/results/final/0.main_table.csv column consensus (TRUE rows) gives 28?

findings.location: Abstract vs Results vs Discussion, Summary of results
findings.evidence: Items reaching consensus: Abstract '38 reached consensus'; Results 'Twenty-six items reached consensus in Round 1' + 'Eight items reached consensus in Round 2' = 34; Discussion 'Consensus was reached for 34 items'. Three different totals for the same quantity.
findings.question_for_authors: How many of the 78 items reached consensus: 38, 34, or another number?

findings.evidence: Paper: 'Twenty-six items reached consensus in Round 1' and 'Forty-four items did not reach consensus'. The authors' stored table results/final/0.main_table.csv has 78 item rows: consensus==TRUE in 28 rows, consensus.1==TRUE in 8 rows, consensus==FALSE and consensus.1==FALSE in 39 rows. 28 + 8 = 36 items reached consensus and 39 did not; 26 + 8 + 44 = 78 only if Round 1 consensus is 26, which the stored table does not show. [Red (build_passport.py, archive_verified): the verification stage printed the authors' stored value with an executed check and upheld the conflict.]
findings.question_for_authors: Which table produced the reported 26 Round-1 and 44 non-consensus counts, given that results/final/0.main_table.csv gives 28 and 39?

findings.evidence: Paper: 'the median absolute change in the percentage of participants that rated an item as essential was 3.8%, and the median absolute difference in participants' rating of an item was 0.15' (also 5.3% and 0.24 for instructor vs academic, 1.3% and 0.06 for initial vs final). Code computes mean(abs(...)): manuscript.Rmd:700 mean(abs(compare_rounds$perc_essential_compare))*100, :701 mean(abs(compare_rounds$mean_compare)), :704-705 and :708-709 the same for the other two comparisons. No median() call appears in these lines, so the reported 'median absolute' statistics are means of absolute differences.
findings.question_for_authors: Were the reported absolute differences computed as means rather than medians, and if so should the text say 'mean absolute change'?

findings.evidence: Paper: 'Of the 47 items included in both Round 1 and Round 2'. The stored table's consensus_dif column marks 41 rows 'stable', 4 'changed', 1 'NA' (a Round-1 non-consensus item with no Round-2 value) and 7 'new_question' (added after Round 1): 41 + 4 + 1 = 46 items have both a Round-1 and a Round-2 consensus value, not 47.
findings.question_for_authors: Which items make up the 47 items included in both rounds?

findings.evidence: Paper: 'Two of the items reaching consensus in Round 2 were added after Round 1 was complete, and two others had already reached consensus among the final sample of 103 participants (but not among the 139 who completed Round 1).' The stored table's consensus_dif column marks 4 Round-2 consensus items 'changed' (Round 1 FALSE -> Round 2 TRUE) and 2 'new_question' (no Round-1 value), i.e. 2 added items and 4 items that shifted, not 2 + 2.
findings.question_for_authors: How many of the Round-2 consensus items were newly added and how many shifted from non-consensus?

findings.evidence: 'A follow-up survey of 46 heads of department in 2023 found that 31 of these 34 items were already taught at their institutions.' No data file, code, table or supplementary item for this follow-up survey exists in the materials (data_src/ holds only the Delphi files 1-8; code_src/manuscript.Rmd contains no reference to heads of department or a 2023 follow-up).
findings.question_for_authors: Can the follow-up survey data (46 heads of department, 31/34 items taught) be shared, or is it reported elsewhere?
